learning: Iteration 2 showed that moving the row forward raised oval max_error and brought back slalom line losses, so the y=0.03 m row is kept. The next race tests whether the ±0.08 m span removes the line losses while max_error stays near 0.061 m, which would point to controller bias as the remaining limit.
notes: Adopts the Builder's ±0.08 m span at y=0.03 m with 16 mm footprints and 0.6 kg. Weights are rescaled to 25 per metre and kp raised to 8.0 to keep the effective steering gain of iteration 1. ki is reverted to 0.05.
rationale: Iteration 2 (row moved to y=0.05 m, ki 0.05 to 0.3) made the oval max_error worse (0.0613 to 0.0637 m) and brought back slalom line losses (1.0 per run). Iteration 1 (y=0.03 m, ±0.06 m span) had zero line losses and the lowest max_error (0.0610 to 0.0613 m). I therefore revert the row to y=0.03 m and follow the Builder's span test: ±0.08 m, seven sensors at 0.0267 m spacing, 16 mm footprints (about 10.7 mm gaps against a 25 mm tape, so a sensor always covers tape inside the span). Mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m and body unchanged so the span change is isolated. Controller: widening the span to ±0.08 m means the weights, scaled to 25 per metre, are now -2 to 2 across x=±0.08 m. Iteration 1 used 33.3 per metre with kp 6.0, an effective gain of about 200. To keep that same effective gain, kp becomes 8.0 (8 × 25 = 200). ki returns to 0.05 because the iteration 2 bias test raised max_error and the integral change is not supported by evidence. kd stays at 0.3 and base_speed at 1.8, with last_direction line-loss recovery kept. Expected result: line_loss_events near zero on the slalom and s-bend, and max_error near 0.061 m on the oval (this is an expectation, not a measured result).
